generator: Built-in image generation with image references
context: Worked examples from a portfolio sticker session on 2026-10-15–16. Image assets are resized display copies.
notes: Prompts are historical run records. Use references/prompt-template.md for new tasks; its explicit image-role mapping resolves older ordinal wording.

items.title: Fieldwork, very close up
items.story: The four little paper researchers work together to hold one ridiculously oversized magnifying glass over a tiny daisy. One braces the handle, one leans over the rim, one crouches on tiptoe and one peers through the lens, where its eye looks comically bigger. The single tiny daisy has an ochre center. Tight playful connected composition, no landscape or background.
items.prompt:
Make ONE witty, collectible die-cut sticker with a clear little visual joke. It is a playful editorial illustration printed on matte sticker paper: one expressive, compact mini-scene with a strong readable silhouette. Allow charming asymmetry, an unexpected pose and the gentle absurdity of the story. The images supplied identify the project character/brand and the approved physical sticker finish. Preserve the character's recognizable identity, while changing its action and composition freely.
Keep a narrow continuous WHITE cut-paper border around the whole mini-scene, like a real sticker (about 22-30px at 1536px). Subtle tactile paper/print texture. The sticker is flat and facing the viewer, with soft daylight on the paper. Square PNG 1536x1536, true transparent alpha outside the border, centered and fully visible with generous margins. No rectangular background or caption, no lettering or watermark. Give the scene life; keep props few and the visual gag immediate.

PROJECT STYLE: The Qunxue mark in reference 1 consists of four different asymmetrical charcoal paper fragments. Turn those FOUR exact fragment silhouettes into a little recurring cast of paper researchers: tiny ivory dot eyes, very simple ink-line arms and legs, no clothing. Each character's body stays one of the original four shapes. Their collaboration creates the joke. Warm editorial CUT-PAPER / INK COLLAGE, mostly graphite and ivory with one small ochre or dusty terracotta accent. Tactile paper edges, lively simple gestures. The flower reference is the physical white-border finish only.

items.title: A little help from your colleagues
items.story: The four paper researchers stack into an awkward but cheerful little HUMAN LADDER to reach one tiny ochre four-point star. Each has a distinct original logo-fragment body. The bottom character is visibly trying to balance, the top one stretches a tiny arm, the other two help each other. Big simple gestures, one connected diagonal silhouette, just the four figures and one star.

items.title: Studying relationships
items.story: The four paper researchers are investigating one soft dusty-terracotta thread, but have accidentally tangled themselves in it. One holds the beginning proudly, one is wrapped once around the waist, one ducks under a loop and one studies the final knot with a tiny magnifier. The line connects them into a lively small social-network knot. Humorous, sparse, clear silhouettes; one continuous white sticker contour.

items.title: An important interview
items.story: The four paper researchers conduct an earnest but funny TIN-CAN TELEPHONE interview: two face each other holding little ivory cups connected by a short curved string, a third leans in to listen, the fourth holds a tiny blank note card upside down. Preserve the four distinct body shapes. Group the figures tightly so their little arms and the string connect the scene, with no floor or background.

items.title: Lost in a good book
items.story: One warm-ivory OPEN BOOK is much bigger than the four paper researchers. They peek out from different places among its pages as if it is a shared hideout: two heads above the pages, one clings to the outer cover, one hangs upside down from a page edge. Tiny calm dot eyes and playful postures. No words on pages. A single compact book-shaped white-edged sticker.

items.title: Eight hands, one deadline
items.story: The little cobalt-blue octopus is busily typing on a tiny charcoal typewriter with four arms, folding one ivory paper airplane with two other arms, and holding a small coffee cup in one curled arm. Its last arm reaches for the messenger bag. It has a focused but slightly overwhelmed face, three tiny blue ink freckles on one cheek. Make this readable and charming rather than busy: octopus is the hero, typewriter is small, one airplane and one cup only. No letters on the paper or keys.

items.title: The inbox wins
items.story: A comically oversized but compact pile of five ivory envelopes has almost buried the little blue octopus. Only its two amused eyes and rounded head show above the pile, while a few mint-tipped arms poke from the sides to keep the envelopes from sliding. One arm gives a tiny satisfied wave. Charcoal messenger bag hangs from one side with the small brand arrow symbol. Warm funny 'too much to publish' moment, no envelope lettering.

A restrained blue/green strip of paper on the plane recalls the brand arrows. Big airy diagonal silhouette, no sky or background.

items.title: A routing problem
items.story: The little blue octopus is arranging three envelopes in a fan, but has tied two of its own mint-tipped arms into a soft loose knot in the middle. It looks at the knot with a small comically puzzled expression while one free arm still proudly holds a perfectly folded paper airplane. Keep three envelopes touching its arms, one airplane and the messenger bag, simple rounded composition and gentle humor, no text.

A compact cozy vignette celebrating the end of a long publishing session, no written label on the box.

items.title: A little too much wind-up
items.story: A single little clockwork bird has wound itself too enthusiastically: the oversized TWO-LOOP winding key sticking from its back is whirling like a tiny helicopter rotor and has accidentally lifted the whole bird. The little bird dangles at a crooked angle, both thin feet hanging and one wing spread for balance, looking sideways at its own key with a small baffled eye. Two or three short ochre motion strokes make the rotating key immediately legible. The key stays visibly attached to the back. A simple funny off-balance silhouette: key above, plump bird and dangling feet below. No scenery.
items.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE playful, tactile die-cut paper sticker for Windup, a 2D character animation tool. The brand's actual logo is a little side-profile mechanical bird. Develop this BIRD into a recurring illustrated character, with a clear little comic action. Reference image 1 is the ORIGINAL WINDUP LOGO: preserve the plump slanted charcoal body, rounded head, small pointed beak, long split pointed tail, and the distinct inset teardrop-shaped wing with a circular hinge and two diagonal strokes. Add two very thin ink-line bird legs and one small expressive ivory eye with a dark dot pupil. The wing is an oatmeal paper panel with two charcoal diagonal strokes and a small ochre hinge. A simple ochre two-loop wind-up key fits into its back. Body remains recognizably the original logo silhouette, not a generic fluffy sparrow. Reference image 2 is a STYLE AND PAPER-FINISH reference ONLY: borrow its warm cut-paper / ink-and-gouache editorial drawing, subtle tactile printed color, charming slight asymmetry, simple gestures and narrow white die-cut border. Do not import its rectangular researchers, magnifying glass, flower, character count or scene. Use only charcoal, warm ivory and a restrained ochre/brass accent. Matte printed illustration, not glossy 3D, not a metal product photo, not a doll. No anime character, human face, hat, clothing or purple witch. Flat front-facing physical paper sticker, one cohesive compact mini-scene. A narrow continuous crisp WHITE paper border around the entire scene, about 18-24px on a 1536px canvas. A little paper-edge thickness, not puffy. Centered and fully visible, generous margins, square 1536x1536 PNG, TRUE TRANSPARENT ALPHA outside the border. No rectangular card or scenery, no floor shadow, no caption, letters, watermark or extra decorative confetti. Favor the readable gesture and gentle absurdity of the story over detail.

items.title: Caught in its own animation
items.story: The little clockwork bird is proudly pulling a short curling IVORY ANIMATION STRIP with its beak, but the loose paper strip has looped once around its own thin ankle. It lifts that foot in comic confusion, leaning backward to keep balance. The strip has exactly three simple drawn frames with small charcoal silhouettes of the same bird in different wing positions, without text, numbers or film sprocket holes. One connected compact S-shaped composition. The back winding key remains small and recognizable here.
